Subject: Req: Dedicated footprint estimate + SLO headroom

Hi Nikhil —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our infra and SRE teams: we anticipate steady-state traffic of ~420 tokens/sec with 3 x 30-minute peak bursts per day that could reach 1,200 tokens/sec for short periods. Our target SLO is 99th percentile inference latency <= 200ms for the primary text-completion route (seq len ~512) and <= 300ms for fallback/longer sequences.

Can you provide a short, conservative dedicated-capacity sizing proposal: tokens/sec -> GPUs mapping, assumed model variant (quantization), expected 99p latency numbers, and recommended headroom (safety margin) for both steady-state and burst? We also want a fallback routing suggestion if dedicated capacity is saturated (e.g., region-level fallback to hosted instances or lower-cost quantized variant).

We're on a tight procurement cadence — ideally a sizing and cost sketch by EOD Friday (14th). Contracts will follow if numbers look reasonable.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of Platform, Polaris AI

Sam —

Quick initial read below, will follow with a spreadsheet and sim results attached (polaris_estimate_v2.xlsx, latency-sim-report.pdf). High level summary up front:

- Steady-state (~420 tps): recommend a pool of 8 T4-equivalent GPUs (or 5 A10x/Q8 variants) with 25% safety margin (N+2 style buffer). Estimated 99p latency: ~140–180ms depending on batching and KV cache hit rate.
- Burst headroom (1,200 tps): enable burst pool + autoscale to add ~10 additional GPUs for up to 10 minutes; this gives transient headroom to keep 99p <= 220ms under our conservative throughput envelope.
- Model variant &q: suggest 8-bit quantized (Q8) for primary; keep FP16 for a canary group for quality checks. Quantization gives ~2–2.5x token/sec per GPU.
- Fallback routing: primary -> Dedicated pool in us-west; if capacity exhausted, fallback to hosted replica in us-east with reduced-cost quantized variant and an automatic notify + degrade-notice header to clients.

Open items: exact kernel/sequence-length profile, target KV cache hit rate (we assumed 60%), and acceptable tokenization overhead for your prompt patterns.

I'll loop Rishi and Laura for ops and SLA math, and get a formal breakdown by EOD Friday.

Cheers,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Nikhil / Marissa —

Quick ops note after scanning Nikhil's sim:

- The 25% safety margin for steady-state is reasonable, but for the described burst shape (3x/day short peaks) we should size burst autoscaling to hit 95% capacity within 90s of ramp. That implies a warm pool of 4 GPUs (standby) + spin-up budget for 6 GPUs.
- For latency math: our sims with sequence distribution (20% > 512, 70% 128–512, 10% <128) show 99p at ~160ms on A10x Q8 for steady-state when batching is enabled with max-batch=16 and target latency budget 100ms for compute. If KV cache hit rate drops to 40% 99p goes to ~210ms — call this our risk scenario.
- Recommendation: include an operational SLA addendum that defines acceptable KV cache hit thresholds and a runbook: if observed 99p > 220ms for 10m, auto-failover to hosted fallback and open incident with both parties.

I'll add the warm-pool sizing and runbook text to the spreadsheet. Marissa — can you draft the SLA addendum paragraph?

-Laura

Sam —

Appended is a short, conservative proposal and next steps. See attached files and Drive link for full sims. TL;DR numbers below (conservative):

- Steady-state pool: 8 A10x-equivalent GPUs running Q8 quantized model (assumes ~60% KV cache hit). Estimated 99p latency: 160ms.
- Burst strategy: warm pool of 4 GPUs + autoscale up to +10 GPUs for bursts (target spin-up to 95% in 90s). Under full burst, 99p ~ 210–230ms depending on cache; hosted fallback route keeps tail <= 300ms.
- Safety margin: provision N+2 for hardware failures and an operational token buffer of 30% headroom above steady-state.
- Fallback: automatic route to hosted us-east replica running a slightly more aggressive quantization profile; add degrade header and customer-facing rate-limit guidance.

Next steps we propose:
1) Review the attached polaris_estimate_v2.xlsx and sign off on the warm-pool and failover acceptance criteria.
2) I’ll generate a DocuSign PO/commit once we lock the warm-pool counts and length of burst window (we used 10 minutes).
3) Ops review call (30m) to agree runbook and KV cache monitoring thresholds.

If that works, I'll get legal/finance to prepare a dedicated commit term sheet and circulate DocuSign link.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this week.

Best,
